Once the players made the bridge they have to make a picture that says SOS so the players have to find paint. the next monster He is earth so he makes earthquakes and he hides in flowers and if he gets you you are dead. once the players found the paint they have to make a helicopter so they have to find scrap. the fourth monster comes out the monster is air and will turn you into wind for 15 seconds. once the players build the helicopter they won the can hide from monsters with boxes. at the end there's a cute seen the fire monster crying. the end

answers.ask: Are the four elemental stages one continuous forest you walk through, or separate chapter maps that load one at a time?
answers.answer: Make it one continuous magical forest that players walk through, with each elemental monster appearing as the players reach the next objective area.

answers.ask: How big should each stage be — a clearing you can see across, or minutes of walking between them?
answers.answer: Keep each stage small, like a clearing or short forest path players can see across, so the game stays easy to play.

config.genre_evidence: Players traverse "one continuous magical forest" while avoiding elemental monsters that "kill player," "chase" players, and require hiding "with boxes." Progress is structured around survival objectives: finding bulbs, wood, paint, and scrap to build items and reach the ending.

extras.text: Place sequential objective stations for assembling the lamp, bridge, SOS sign, and helicopter along the route.

config.addendum:
LAYOUT FEATURES for this Survival map. Build these as the actual structure of the space rather than as set dressing, keep them visually distinct from one another, and keep the whole layout legible in one view.

SHAPE OF THE SPACE - Guided Route: A single directed route through one continuous space, sequencing the player past its key moments rather than letting them wander.

INCLUDE:
- Crawlspaces & Lockers: Small localized cutouts built into lower walls where players break enemy sightlines and hide. Minimum 4 studs on the entry axis (Part I §2).
- Water Body: Standing or flowing water as a real feature of the map — a lake, river, sea, or pool — whether swum through or treated as a barrier.
